এস. আর. ও. নং ২৫১-আইন/২০২২/১৩৩/কাস্টমস।—যেহেতু পারস্পরিক বাণিজ্য সম্প্রসারণের লক্ষ্যে Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) এর আওতাধীন Framework Agreement on Trade Preferential System among the Member States of the Organization of the Islamic Conference (TPS-OIC) শীর্ষক চুক্তি, অতঃপর উক্ত চুক্তি বলিয়া উল্লিখিত, গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রী বাংলাদেশ স্বাক্ষর ও অনুসমর্থন করিয়াছে; এবং

যেহেতু উক্ত চুক্তির Article 3 এর clause (1) এর উদ্দেশ্যপূরণকল্পে, উহার Article 5 এর clause (1) ও (2) এ বর্ণিত Concession List অনুযায়ী, চুক্তিবদ্ধ দেশসমূহের আমদানি শুল্কহার হ্রাস করিবার বিধান রহিয়াছে; এবং

যেহেতু উক্ত চুক্তির আওতায় স্বাক্ষরিত Protocol on the Preferential Tariff Scheme for TPS-OIC (PRETAS), অতঃপর উক্ত Protocol বলিয়া উল্লিখিত, এবং TPS-OIC Rules of Origin অনুযায়ী বাংলাদেশ কর্তৃক Concession List অনুমোদন ও প্রেরণ করা হইয়াছে;

সেহেতু সরকার, Customs Act, 1969 (Act No. IV of 1969) এর section 19 এর sub-section (1)-এ প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতাবলে, জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ডের সহিত পরামর্শক্রমে, জনস্বার্থে, উক্ত Act এর FIRST SCHEDULE-ভুক্ত পণ্যসমূহের মধ্যে নিম্নের TABLE এর কলাম (১) এর Sl. No. এর বিপরীতে কলাম (২) এ বর্ণিত H.S Code-সমূহের আওতাভুক্ত কলাম (৩) এ উল্লিখিত পণ্যের উপর আরোপণীয় আমদানি শুল্কের যে পরিমাণ কলাম (৫) এ বর্ণিত হারের অতিরিক্ত হয় সেই পরিমাণ হইতে, উক্ত Protocol এ বর্ণিত সময় সীমার জন্য, Annex I এ বর্ণিত অংশগ্রহণকারী দেশসমূহে উৎপাদিত ও প্রক্রিয়াজাতকৃত পণ্যের ক্ষেত্রে, Annex II এ বর্ণিত TPS-OIC Rules of Origin-তে বর্ণিত শর্তাবলি প্রতিপালন সাপেক্ষে, অব্যাহতি প্রদান করিল, যথা:—

First Schedule: The schedule contains the list of goods subject to import duties which are impacted by the preferential duty rate changes introduced under the TPS-OIC agreement.
Imported Goods or Raw Materials: A specified list of goods identified by H.S. Codes in the table are granted a concessional customs duty rate when imported from participating countries under the TPS-OIC agreement. This duty concession applies to the portion of the rate that exceeds the rates specifically provided in the notification, provided the goods meet the applicable rules of origin requirements.
National Board of Revenue: The Government consults with this body before issuing notifications that grant customs duty exemptions or concessions.

Customs Duty: The application of customs duty rates is specified for goods within a tariff heading where the term Exclusively Applicable implies that the duty rate pertains solely to the specific item described in the relevant table column, even if the HS Code covers multiple types of goods.
H.S. Code: The HS Code is used to categorize goods, and specific customs duty rates are restricted to individual items within these codes when marked as exclusively applicable in the official table.
TABLE: The table provides a structured framework for defining the scope of customs duty application by mapping specific goods to their respective duty rates, utilizing designations such as exclusively applicable to clarify tax liabilities for items under a shared HS Code.

Customs Notification: This clause specifies that the provisions of the current statutory regulatory order shall take effect immediately upon its issuance.

Annex-II
TRADE PREFERENTIAL SYSTEM AMONG THE MEMBER STATES OF
THE ORGANISATION OF THE ISLAMIC CONFERENCE (TPS-OIC)

TPS-OIC RULES OF ORIGIN

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS

Trade Preferential System among the Memb: This instrument governs the trade preferential system established among member states of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation.
Rules of Origin: These regulations establish the criteria and requirements for determining the origin of goods traded under the preferential system.

processed_clauses.resolved_text:
Article 1
Scope

1. This document is called "TPS-OIC Rules of Origin"

2. TPS-OIC Rules of Origin shall be applied for determining the origin of products eligible for preferential concessions under the Framework Agreement on Trade Preferential System Among the Member States of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference (Hereinafter referred to as Framework Agreement) and the Protocol on Preferential Tariff Scheme (Hereinafter referred to as PRETAS).

Trade Preferential System among the Memb: These rules establish the criteria for determining the origin of products that are eligible for preferential duty concessions under the Trade Preferential System among the Member States of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference.
The rules govern the application of preferential concessions as provided for under both the Framework Agreement and the Protocol on Preferential Tariff Scheme.
Rules of Origin: The document is titled TPS-OIC Rules of Origin and provides the legal framework for determining the originating status of goods under the specified trade agreements.

Harmonized System: This system refers to the Harmonized Commodity Description and Coding System, which provides the nomenclature of chapters and tariff headings used for the classification of goods.
Classification of Goods: This process refers to assigning a product or material under a specific heading within the Harmonized System.
Consignment: A consignment consists of products sent simultaneously from one exporter to one consignee, documented either by a single transport document or a single invoice.
Customs Value: Customs value is primarily defined as the transaction value or the price paid for imported goods including leviable charges and adjustments.

When transaction value is unavailable, customs value is determined using alternative methods including the value of identical or similar goods, the deductive value method, the computed value method, or the fall-back method.
Goods: The term goods encompasses both materials and finished products.
Manufacturer: The process of manufacture includes any working or processing, such as assembly or specific operations, applied to both industrial and agricultural products.
Raw Materials: Materials are defined as any ingredients, components, parts, or raw materials utilized in the production of a final product.
Ex-works Price: The ex-works price is the price paid to the manufacturer for a product at the factory gate, including the value of all materials used but excluding any internal taxes that may be repaid upon export.
Value Added: Value added is calculated by subtracting the customs value of non-originating materials from the ex-works price of the final product.

processed_clauses.resolved_text:
Article 3
General Requirements

Products covered by preferential trading arrangements under the Framework Agreement imported into the territory of a Participating State from another Participating State which are consigned directly within the meaning of Article 13 hereof, shall be eligible for preferential concessions if they conform to the origin requirement under any one of the following conditions:

a) products wholly produced or obtained in the exporting Participating State as defined in Article 4; or

(b) products obtained in a Participating State incorporating materials which have not been wholly obtained there, provided that such materials have undergone sufficient working or processing in that Participating State within the meaning of Article 5.

Imported Goods: Products imported under preferential trading arrangements from a participating state to another are eligible for preferential concessions if they meet specific origin requirements.

To qualify, goods must be consigned directly from the exporting state and satisfy either the criteria for products wholly produced in that state or the criteria for goods with non-originating materials that have undergone sufficient working or processing.

Wholly Produced or Obtained Products: These are defined as goods derived entirely from a specific exporting Participating State, including mineral resources, agricultural harvests, livestock, and fishing or aquaculture products.

The category also encompasses items produced on factory ships using originating marine resources, used articles collected for raw material recovery, manufacturing waste, and final goods manufactured exclusively from these qualifying originating materials.
Export: The clause outlines the origin criteria for products exported from a Participating State, establishing that goods must be entirely produced or obtained within that territory to qualify under these provisions.
